brief.prompt: Make a pitch deck for Tesla

questions.question: Who is in the room, and what do they already believe about Tesla?
suggestions: Growth investors who already believe in Tesla's EV and energy story
Skeptical institutional investors worried about competition and valuation
Fleet or enterprise buyers who haven't yet considered switching to Tesla

questions.question: What should the audience do at the end of the pitch?
suggestions: Commit capital to the next funding round
Approve a pilot or fleet purchase order
Book a follow-up meeting with the leadership team

questions.question: What is the one sentence they must remember?
suggestions: Tesla is an energy and AI company, not just a carmaker
Tesla's cost advantage and software lead make its growth durable
Tesla's vertical integration lets it scale faster than any rival

questions.question: What proof do you have to back this up?
suggestions: Delivery and revenue figures, fleet data, and customer or analyst quotes

questions.question: How many minutes do you have, and are you presenting live or sending it?
suggestions: Sent as a self-explanatory read-ahead deck

outline.governing_thought: Tesla can win the shift to electric transport by growing energy storage alongside vehicles as competition intensifies.
key_points: Transport is a quarter of fuel combustion CO2 and road emissions are still rising
Electric car demand is accelerating toward 40% of global sales by 2030
Tesla's storage deployments more than doubled in 2024 while vehicle deliveries slipped 1%

fields.name: headline
fields.text: Transport emits a quarter of the world's fuel CO2

fields.name: kicker
fields.text: The stakes

fields.name: stat-label
fields.text: Share of global CO2 from fuel combustion that came from transport in 2024

slides.notes: We start with the scale of the problem. One quarter of the world's CO2 from burning fuel comes from moving people and goods, according to the IEA's 2024 data. That is a share we cannot ignore if we want to bring emissions down. Power generation and industry get most of the attention, but transport touches every household and every supply chain. So any serious climate plan has to include how we get around, and that is the lens for everything we cover today.

fields.name: headline
fields.text: Road emissions keep climbing, up 8% since 2015

fields.name: kicker
fields.text: Problem

fields.name: point-1
fields.text: Road transport emitted just over 6 Gt of CO2 in 2024

fields.name: stat-label
fields.text: Rise in road transport CO2 emissions from 2015 to 2024

fields.name: source
fields.text: IEA Breakthrough Agenda Report 2025, 2024

slides.notes: Within transport, roads are where the pressure sits. The IEA Breakthrough Agenda Report 2025 puts road emissions at just over 6 gigatonnes of CO2 in 2024. The more worrying part is the direction. Emissions are 8% higher than in 2015, so a decade of efficiency gains and policy has not turned the curve. More vehicles and more driving have outrun the improvements. That tells us incremental fixes are not enough, and it leads to the next question: is the shift to electric happening fast enough?

fields.name: headline
fields.text: Electric cars now make up over a quarter of sales

fields.name: kicker
fields.text: Why now

fields.name: stat
fields.text: 20 million

fields.name: stat-label
fields.text: Electric cars the IEA expects to be sold worldwide in 2025

fields.name: source
fields.text: IEA Global EV Outlook 2025, 2025

slides.notes: The answer is that it is happening, and at real scale. The IEA's Global EV Outlook 2025 expects around 20 million electric cars to be sold worldwide in 2025. That is no longer a niche market or an early-adopter story. Electric cars are now a mainstream choice for buyers across many markets. For us, that matters because it means the demand side of this transition is no longer hypothetical. The question has moved from whether it will happen to who captures the growth.

fields.name: headline
fields.text: Electric car demand is still accelerating

fields.name: kicker
fields.text: Momentum

fields.name: point-1
fields.text: Record first-quarter sales in all major markets

fields.name: stat-label
fields.text: Year-on-year rise in global electric car sales in Q1 2025

fields.name: source
fields.text: IEA Global EV Outlook 2025, 2025

slides.notes: Momentum is still building. The IEA's Global EV Outlook 2025 reports global electric car sales up 35% year on year in the first quarter of 2025. Just as important, that quarter set records in every major market, so this is not one region carrying the numbers. When a market this large is still growing at that pace, the tailwind is structural. That is the backdrop for Tesla's position, which we turn to next.

fields.name: headline
fields.text: Tesla answers with electric vehicles and energy storage

fields.name: kicker
fields.text: Solution

fields.name: point-1
fields.text: Electric vehicles for the road

fields.name: point-2
fields.text: Energy storage deployments alongside them

slides.notes: So where does Tesla fit? We see two parts to the answer. The first is the one everyone knows: electric vehicles for the road. The second is easier to overlook: energy storage, deployed alongside those vehicles. Both rest on the same battery know-how, and both serve a world that is electrifying. Our argument today is that the two together, not vehicles alone, give Tesla its strongest path as the market grows and gets more crowded. Let us look at how each is performing.

fields.name: headline
fields.text: Tesla more than doubled its energy storage deployments in 2024

fields.name: kicker
fields.text: Traction

fields.name: point-1
fields.text: Up from 14.7 GWh in 2023

fields.name: stat
fields.text: 31.4 GWh

fields.name: stat-label
fields.text: Energy storage deployed by Tesla in 2024

fields.name: source
fields.text: Tesla (SEC Exhibit 99.1, Q4 2024 update), 2024

slides.notes: Start with storage, because this is where the momentum is. Tesla's Q4 2024 update, filed with the SEC as Exhibit 99.1, shows 31.4 gigawatt-hours deployed in 2024. In 2023 the figure was 14.7. So deployments more than doubled in a single year. That is the kind of growth we expect from a business that is scaling, not just holding its position. It also shows Tesla can turn its battery capability into a second line of business.

fields.name: headline
fields.text: Tesla delivered more than 1.7 million vehicles in 2024

fields.name: kicker
fields.text: Traction

fields.name: point-1
fields.text: Deliveries slipped 1% as competition intensified

fields.name: stat-label
fields.text: Vehicles Tesla delivered in 2024

fields.name: source
fields.text: Illustrative; Tesla (SEC Exhibit 99.1, Q4 2024 update), 2024

slides.notes: Now the vehicle side. Tesla's Q4 2024 update, SEC Exhibit 99.1, shows 1,789,226 deliveries in 2024, though we should flag that the slide marks this figure as illustrative. That is still a very large base. But deliveries slipped 1% from the prior year, and that happened while the overall electric market kept growing. The cause is competition: more rivals, more choice for buyers. So vehicles remain the foundation, but they are no longer the source of easy growth.

fields.name: headline
fields.text: Electric cars are heading for 40% of global sales by 2030

fields.name: kicker
fields.text: Market

fields.name: point-1
fields.text: China is already near 60% of car sales in 2025

fields.name: stat-label
fields.text: Share of global car sales the IEA projects for electric cars in 2030

fields.name: source
fields.text: IEA Global EV Outlook 2025, 2030; IEA Global EV Outlook 2025, 2025

slides.notes: The market itself is not the problem. The IEA's Global EV Outlook 2025 projects electric cars reaching 40% of global car sales by 2030. China shows what that looks like in practice: it is already near 60% of car sales in 2025. That is a preview of where other markets are heading. A bigger market is good news, but it is also a magnet for competitors, which is the pressure we turn to next.

fields.name: headline
fields.text: Rivals and falling prices are squeezing vehicle growth

fields.name: kicker
fields.text: Competition

fields.name: point-1
fields.text: Falling electric car prices are a factor in China

fields.name: point-2
fields.text: Storage gives Tesla a second growth engine

slides.notes: Here is the tension. In China, falling electric car prices are one factor in the squeeze, and rivals are keen to take share. Tesla cannot assume a growing market will carry its vehicle volumes along with it. That is why storage matters so much. It gives Tesla a second growth engine that does not depend on winning every price war in car showrooms. Growth in one line can offset pressure in the other, and that balance is the heart of our thesis.

fields.name: headline
fields.text: Back Tesla's push to grow storage alongside vehicles

fields.name: kicker
fields.text: The ask

fields.name: point-1
fields.text: Electric demand is rising and competition is intensifying

fields.name: point-2
fields.text: Storage doubled in 2024 while vehicle deliveries slipped 1%

fields.name: source
fields.text: Tesla (SEC Exhibit 99.1, Q4 2024 update), 2024

slides.notes: So what are we asking for? Back Tesla's push to grow storage alongside vehicles. The case is simple. Electric demand keeps rising, and competition keeps intensifying. Tesla's own Q4 2024 update, SEC Exhibit 99.1, shows storage more than doubling in 2024 while vehicle deliveries slipped 1%. Those two trends point in the same direction. Supporting both lines gives Tesla the best chance to win the shift to electric transport, and we would like your support for that strategy.
